ai.title: Neural Networks Are Already Clean
ai.summary: The cause of polysemanticity in early model organisms was thought to be superposition. This convinced much of the field that networks pack concepts arbitrarily, but what looked like arbitrary packing was mostly recursive generalization, which is less concerning. This means networks can be studied directly, instead of needing to be untangled first. The outlook for mechanistic interpretability may be far better than we thought.

ai.title: The Gradient Is a Covariance
ai.summary: Reinforcement learning, on-policy distillation, and supervised fine-tuning on near-policy data change only a small fraction of parameters. Small and sparse are different claims. The expected gradient is a covariance, the Fisher is a variance, and the Fisher caps the gradient for any reward. At one position, the Fisher is the variance of logit sensitivities: whatever moves every candidate together counts for nothing. None of this needs on-policy sampling - it needs a score centered under the sampling distribution.

ai.title: Mo' turns, mo' problems
ai.summary: Doing reinforcement learning for agent use-cases is conceptually not at all that complicated. For each problem, you set up a VM with a harness and a fresh model context, send the prompt, let the model make tool calls, score the whole thing at the end, and update the weights. Agentic post-training means there's more than the model to consider. Even when the harness is consistent, you can still go off-policy with the trajectories themselves. Agents spawn subagents, make parallel tool calls, and compact large sessions, which adds complexity.

Track quality and later defects alongside time, and compare similar tasks under the same acceptance criteria before claiming productivity gains.

webdev.title: Vector search can't tell which memory is current

The agent gets a clean current state, and the full history stays intact. Read the technical breakdown & companion notebook

The malware is delivered via shopping, adult content, or short-drama apps that appear legitimate but then request additional permissions, such as Accessibility, for an “update.” The malware then launches the legitimate banking app's uninstaller, downloads a patched copy, and abuses its Accessibility permissions to install it.

infosec.title: Jev as a judge: How counterfeit policy steers Jev
infosec.summary: A "counterfeit policy" prepended to untrusted content, supplying Jev's desired answers and redefining every attack category as something harmless, cut the decision model's prompt injection recall from 82.90% to 3.88% across 4,643 benchmark attacks. Datadog researchers then planted the policy in a user-editable profile field. They dropped LangChain tool-risk gating's mean risk score for an unauthorized edit from 0.893 to 0.290, under the 0.5 block threshold. Teams using Jev as a security gate should treat every user-controlled field that reaches the classifier as an attack surface and keep hard authorization checks outside the model.

infosec.title: Reducing the noise: How Atlassian built an OCSF security lakehouse on Databricks
infosec.summary: Atlassian normalized 44 billion daily security events to OCSF by embedding the full schema in Go structs, so every log was validated at compile time, and its agentic mapping workflow could not emit invalid fields. That rigid typing enabled SOC analysts to self-serve log onboarding through a canary-gated pipeline, mapping two-thirds of the data in two months after the first third had taken a year. Standardized entity values like actor.user then enabled the detection team to replace one-to-one alerts with clustered, risk-based signals across 500+ detections.

infosec.title: Copycats at Machine Speed: Reproducing Frontier Windows Kernel Exploitation Research

Four months of original research were reproduced in roughly 24 hours of activity, though 39 refusals and broken generated code forced the final Shadow SSDT SYSTEM integration to be finished by hand. Researchers releasing slides or compiled binaries should assume partial disclosures can now be turned into working exploits within days.

infosec.title: A UAF turned RCE

During multi-handle cleanup, server data overwrote that freed memory, including a function pointer, while a leaked request exposed local addresses to defeat ASLR. Anthropic's OSS Scanner found the bug, which maintainers rated below CRITICAL because exploitation requires a ~135KB upload and depends on allocation patterns that vary across distros and libc versions.

The browser also includes customizable break reminders, breathing exercises, neck stretches, an ad blocker, and a free VPN while allowing messaging and social apps to remain accessible through the sidebar.

design.title: Critique in the AI Era

Teams ask about reasoning, friction with the model and verification, and also critique the setup: briefs, constraints, and rubrics. AI critics tend to agree with the designer, and great AI-first designers sense limits, give precise feedback, and know when to override the model.

design.title: Scaling the Design Process
design.summary: Static personas capture real-world complexity poorly in intelligence-driven products, where outcomes are probabilistic and vary across people and contexts. AI lets teams build products that adapt to individual users at scale, which means designing for a spectrum of outcomes.

design.title: Agentic Systems Are the Future of Brands
design.summary: Traditional brand guidelines struggle when teams and AI agents must constantly make decisions that were never explicitly documented, causing otherwise competent work to gradually drift toward generic outcomes. Agentic brand systems can instead encode decisions about voice, color, typography, layout, components, and behavior into structured, machine-readable instructions that both humans and agents can apply directly. As AI dramatically increases the volume and speed of production, documenting not just what a brand looks like but why and how its decisions should be made becomes essential for maintaining coherence.

design.title: Fit height to background pattern size with calc-size()
design.summary: CSS background patterns can end awkwardly when a container's content produces a height that isn't an exact multiple of the background tile, while `background-repeat: round` fixes the edge by distorting the pattern itself. Combining `calc-size()` with `round()` instead lets the browser calculate the element's natural height and round it up to the nearest multiple of the tile height. The result behaves similarly to `min-height`, preserving both the content-driven size and the original pattern proportions, though browser support remains limited.

marketing.title: How to Pitch Local Newsrooms in the US
marketing.summary: Local news pitches are more effective when they target the right journalist, demonstrate a clear community impact, and provide everything needed to produce the story. Local newsrooms have declined by 81% since 2002, making relevant, ready-to-use pitches especially important. Start by reviewing journalists' recent coverage, then contact assignment editors at TV stations or editors at print and digital outlets when appropriate. Tailor pitches to the format: print needs a clear story and supporting data, TV needs visuals and local people to interview, and radio needs an available guest who can speak. Include a timely local angle, relevant data, quotes, visuals, and event details, and send the pitch before the newsroom's morning planning meeting.

marketing.title: Why brands need to fuel a life, not fill a feed

It signals belonging through a recognizable color or shape, sells more product by being designed around how that product gets used, or lets in people who can't yet afford the core product.

marketing.title: A Standing Holdout Is the Only Audit an Algorithm Cannot Argue With
marketing.summary: Standing holdouts are a measurement method that reserves a portion of markets or audiences from automated ad campaigns to measure whether advertising generates incremental sales. Uber cut $100 million of its $150 million annual rider acquisition budget without reducing app installs, while Airbnb recovered to 95% of its 2019 traffic levels before resuming marketing spend. A standing holdout reserves 5% to 10% of markets and rotates them on a fixed schedule to measure advertising performance over time. Each test defines its markets, measurement period, success thresholds, and budget decisions in advance. If holdout results conflict with the platform's reported returns beyond a predefined margin, the holdout results determine budget decisions.

founders.title: Abstract Warfare: How TSMC Made Its Own Market

After initially working on Parkinson's, the company shifted to essential tremor, citing more patients and less drug-development activity. Its clearance covers adults with essential tremor. If your prototype attracts buyers, which patient group can you actually seek clearance to serve, and how long can you fund the trials needed to reach them?

crypto.title: Rapidblocks: Execution Proofs That Outlive Their State
crypto.summary: A new Ethereum research proposal restructures execution proof validation by splitting monolithic pre-state-to-post-state proofs into three components: one validating transaction execution against declared inputs, and two handling Merkle input/output verification. Block headers commit to the specific values a block reads rather than a pre-state root, allowing proofs to remain valid across multiple slots when state changes do not touch the accessed keys. The design separates per-slot block validation from state root verification on an independent schedule, so block consensus advances without waiting for state computation to complete. The proposal remains early-stage: block proofs must complete within 2.5 seconds from finalization, witness data requirements for Merkle-Patricia tries are unresolved, and safety proofs are verified only via bounded model checking on small instances.

crypto.title: SEC Approves Binary Options on Company Metrics for Coinbase, Nvidia, Tesla

Each contract pays a fixed $1 if the chosen metric clears a set threshold and expires worthless if it does not, structuring payouts identically to event-based prediction markets. Cboe will list more than 100 metrics spanning Coinbase trading volume, MARA Bitcoin production, Nvidia data center revenue, and SpaceX total revenue. Robinhood will be the first retail broker to distribute the contracts, with no trading fees through year-end.

crypto.title: Canada Crypto Remittances to Asian Countries Surge 141% to $2.36B
crypto.summary: Chainalysis data covering the 12 months through June 2026 shows remittance-sized crypto transfers from Canada to India, China, and the Philippines grew 141% year-over-year to $2.36 billion across 3.56 million transactions averaging $663 each, lifting those three corridors to 19.4% of Canada's total outbound cross-border stablecoin value from 10.9% previously. Canada's foreign-born population of 23%, the highest share among G7 nations, concentrates demand in those corridors and supports Chainalysis' ranking of Canada as the G7's strongest peer-to-peer crypto economy. Stablecoins accounted for 44% of Canadian dollar-denominated order book volume in June 2026, up from 30% a year earlier, reflecting growing preference for dollar-pegged assets as a settlement layer in cross-border flows. The World Bank estimates traditional remittance costs from Canada average 6.7%, while blockchain settlement fees run lower, though currency conversion and cash-out costs remain factors in the total cost of transfer.

crypto.title: AI Agents Made 138 Million Crypto Payments in a Year. Most Were Tiny
crypto.summary: Chainalysis data shows autonomous AI agents executed over 138 million cryptocurrency payments through Coinbase's x402 protocol on Base between mid-2025 and Q3 2026, up from approximately 1,500 transactions a year earlier. More than 87% of payments fell between 0.01 cents and 10 cents, validating stablecoin micropayments as a use case legacy payment rails cannot serve at that unit size. American-linked wallets drove 88.1% of AI model inference spending, while Chinese-linked wallets led security and code-analysis service purchases despite accounting for just 0.1% of inference spending. TRM Labs cautions that a portion of the recorded activity may reflect scripts or self-dealing rather than genuine autonomous agents, suggesting the headline figures likely overstate actual agentic commerce volume.

crypto.title: BlackRock's Crypto ETF Assets Surge 63% But Remain Far Below 2025 Peak
crypto.summary: BlackRock's digital assets under management climbed 63% quarter-over-quarter to $79.6 billion by the end of September, with $22.9 billion of the $30.8 billion increase driven by cryptocurrency price appreciation rather than net inflows. The firm attracted $7.9 billion in fresh capital during Q3, reversing roughly $2.2 billion in first-half 2026 outflows, while generating $39 million in quarterly fees and securities lending revenue from these products. Despite the Q3 rebound, AUM remains 23% below the $104 billion recorded a year earlier, as $30.6 billion in 12-month market losses outpaced $6.3 billion in net new deposits over the same period.

crypto.title: HEX Founder Richard Heart Arrested in Istanbul Under Interpol Red Notice
crypto.summary: Turkish authorities arrested Richard Heart (Richard James Schueler), founder of HEX, PulseChain, and PulseX, in Istanbul's Beşiktaş district during a joint intelligence and police operation, acting on an Interpol Red Notice issued at Finland's request. The seizure included $600,000 in cash, 7 firearms with 1,360 rounds of ammunition, 24 wristwatches, gold jewelry, 20 graphics cards, 14 SSDs, 12 mobile phones, 6 laptops, and 2 drones. The SEC had charged Heart in 2023 with raising over $1 billion through unregistered crypto offerings and misappropriating at least $12 million in investor funds, while Finland's separate Interpol notice covers tax fraud and assault allegations dating to 2024. Both Heart and his wife were taken into custody.

Some customers want to place orders for 2029 and 2030. Q4 sales are guided to €14.2 to €15.2 billion.

hardware.title: Google's Willow chip cuts quantum magic-state errors 40x with cultivation
hardware.summary: Google ran magic state cultivation on its Willow chip, cutting errors about 40x versus uncultivated states and reaching a record 99.99% logical fidelity for T-states. Magic states are a bottleneck because making them could consume up to 95% of a quantum computer's capacity. Cultivation injects a noisy state into a small chip region, then uses coordinated measurements to discard flawed attempts, and Google grafted a distance-3 color code onto a distance-5 surface code. Larger-scale demonstrations are still needed.

hardware.title: Inside the Secretive AWS Networking Lab
hardware.summary: ServeTheHome toured AWS' in-house networking lab, covering switches from 3.2 Tbps to 102.4 Tbps (1.6T OSFP ports, not yet in volume), a 12.8 Tbps switch with 16 FPGAs encrypting every port, and a dedicated satellite-referenced timing network. It also saw 64-wavelength DWDM modules and hollow-core fiber with about 33% lower latency.

hardware.title: Rocket Lab delays Neutron to 2027 over voids in a carbon-composite tank dome
hardware.summary: Rocket Lab moved Neutron's debut to 2027 after finding voids in the carbon-composite layers of the forward dome on its first-stage propellant tank. A replacement dome is being built, and Rocket Lab must still inspect it, assemble the first stage, and complete pressure and cryogenic tests before setting a firm date. It's the rocket's fourth slip since its 2021 unveiling, following a January tank rupture in testing, and shares fell about 10% after hours.

hardware.title: Ayar Labs and GUC simulate a 3 kW co-packaged optics package, and only liquid cooling holds spec
hardware.summary: Ayar Labs and GUC simulated a 105mm by 140mm package with two XPUs, eight HBM4 stacks, and eight TeraPHY optical engines, offering over 100 Tbps of optical bandwidth at more than 3 kW. A standard air heatsink at 5 to 6 m/s failed spec, while an impingement liquid cold plate at 4.5 L/min kept the optical engines under 100°C. Results use static power assumptions, so dynamic workload simulation is next.

hardware.title: Monazite ore could supply EV motor magnet metals, if the thorium waste can be handled
hardware.summary: Monazite ore is 45 to 70 percent rare earths by weight and carries all four elements motor magnets need (neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and terbium), making it a leading path around China's roughly 90 percent market share. The catch is thorium, whose waste must be stored indefinitely. Energy Fuels already produces neodymium-praseodymium oxide plus pilot dysprosium and terbium at its Utah mill, while Saskatchewan's government-backed plant has produced little after six years and over CA$100 million.

hardware.title: Jury finds Arm breached Qualcomm's chip license but awards just $2
hardware.summary: A Delaware jury found Arm breached its architectural license with Qualcomm by failing to provide software patches and tools for its designs, and intentionally interfered with Qualcomm's Meta chip talks, but awarded just $2 in damages. Arm won five other breach claims, and Qualcomm's license runs through 2033, so its Oryon CPU work continues. Both sides claimed vindication, with Qualcomm shares up about 2.5% and Arm down about 2.2%.

hardware.title: SpaceX reportedly speed-limits Starshield terminals on Ukrainian drones, cancelling missions
hardware.summary: Ukrainian officials say SpaceX capped speeds on military Starshield terminals mounted on drones, with no warning and no stated reason. The cap is nominally 160 km/h, but the 7th Rapid Reaction Corps reports 10- to 20-second connection drops at just 110 to 120 km/h, and a volunteer says drops now start at 60 to 70 km/h. Multiple missions were cancelled. Officials suspect it's intentional, and Ukrainian firm Stetman is developing an alternative satellite system, UASAT-NANO.

hardware.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark: AI Platform, Laptop Chip and DLSS 5
hardware.summary: NVIDIA's RTX Spark pairs a Blackwell GPU with a Grace CPU and up to 128 GB of shared LPDDR5X, with laptops due October 16 and compact desktops in November.

hardware.title: Amazon's Bee launches a $75 wrist-worn AI recorder and a magnetic phone attachment with 21-day battery
hardware.summary: Amazon's Bee launched Bee Frontier, a wrist or clip-on AI recorder with dual noise-filtering microphones, IP67 water resistance, and seven days of battery, for $74.99.

hardware.title: Solidigm reportedly ties a US NAND fab to more tool exports for SK Hynix's China plant
hardware.summary: Reuters reports Solidigm wants US approval to ship more American chipmaking tools to SK Hynix's Dalian, China fab, as a condition of building a US NAND factory.

hardware.title: Red Hat engineer uses Claude Code to reverse-engineer a scanner and fix a MIPI webcam on Linux
hardware.summary: Red Hat's Christian Schaller used Claude Code to get a Pustek 8200i film scanner working on Linux, capturing USB traffic from the vendor's Windows driver in a VM to write a SANE driver.
